html:
SMTO-GWT-0059 — The NVIDIA GPU driver reported a problem

GUID: deae4af7-2a74-5755-98c3-2016ee0b3f6b
Slug: gpu-driver-unavailable
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • The NVIDIA tool on the Gateway computer stopped with a driver error. If you asked for a GPU setting change, that error doesn't always prove whether the change took effect.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Gateway computer, open a terminal as the account that runs the Gateway and type nvidia-smi. Note any error it prints. This shows whether the driver problem is on that computer, outside SMTO.
  2. If nvidia-smi shows a driver error, restart the Gateway computer. If the error remains, reinstall or update the NVIDIA graphics driver. Driver errors often follow a driver update that hasn't been finished by a restart.
  3. Ask SMTO to show the GPU status for this Gateway. A clean status reading confirms the driver works again.
  4. If you had asked SMTO to change a GPU setting, ask it to show that GPU's details first, and request the change again only if the setting is still not what you wanted. Some driver errors happen after the change was already applied.

What success looks like

  • nvidia-smi prints your GPUs, and asking SMTO for the GPU status works without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with what nvidia-smi printed, to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't repeat a GPU setting change until you've checked the current setting, and don't stop programs using the GPU to work around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • nvidia-smi exited with a driver-related or unmapped non-zero exit code on the Gateway.

What this means

  • nvidia-smi exited unsuccessfully with a driver-related or otherwise unmapped code. Some unmapped mutation exits retain unknown effects, so this is not proof that configuration stayed unchanged. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • nvidia-smi exited unsuccessfully with a driver-related or otherwise unmapped code. Some unmapped mutation exits retain unknown effects, so this is not proof that configuration stayed unchanged.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect provider exit classification, driver health and the operation's retained effect flag; distinguish a read failure from attempted configuration.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, run nvidia-smi as the Gateway account and check the NVIDIA driver (kernel module loaded, driver/library versions matching, GPU visible; check the system log for driver messages), reinstalling or rebooting if needed. Then run gpu.status; if a configuration change was attempted, read the exact device state for that UUID with gpu.device before submitting another change.
  • Check the Gateway's NVIDIA driver and gpu.status. If configuration was attempted, read the exact device state before another mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Check the Gateway NVIDIA driver and inspect gpu.status.

How to verify the fix

  • Provider queries succeed and any attempted configuration is reconciled for its exact UUID.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
